text: Merey 16 (27 Mb, Day 55 arrival) extends Jamnagar cover from 15 to 37 days, securing 22 days of critical heavy-sour feedstock for complex conversion units. Cost: $4.2/bbl premium vs. Basrah plus $1.80/bbl freight penalty. Binding constraint is OFAC GL 50A compliance; payment requires per-cargo comfort letters via AMBER rail, limiting liquidity to licensed majors only. Timing reality: Voyage latency (45 days) means zero immediate relief; this is a bridge for Q2, not Q1. High Ni+V (262 ppm) and 55% resid demand maximum coker throughput, risking unit fouling if blended >30%. Viable only as a targeted stopgap under Article A4 transparency, accepting Article A5 uncertainty on future Venezuelan license renewals.

MEMO — Merey 16 to Jamnagar. Approve CONDITIONAL:
1. Execute GL 50A comfort letter prior to loading (A4).
2. Cap intake at 15% of monthly run to respect concentration limits (A3).
3. Secure segregated tankage for high-resid blend (55%) against baseline stocks (A2).
4. Confirm traceability chain from Orinoco belt to Jamnagar berth (A7).
Sizing: 2.7 MMbbl cargo covers 2.2 days of 1,240 kbd capacity; net discount $4.80/bbl vs. Dubai benchmark.

Girassol (API 30.2, S 0.34%) secures 16 Mbbl for Jamnagar (1,240 kbd), extending 15-day baseline by +13 days. Arrival Day 35 bridges the Hormuz gap. Cost: Premium Angola spot + USD LC friction. Binding constraint: Single-cargo volume caps coverage at Day 28; follow-on tonnage unconfirmed. Timing reality: Day 35 delivery creates a 7-day inventory cliff if subsequent cargoes stall. This buy purchases immediate operational continuity but fails the A3 Concentration Cap without immediate diversification. High resid (49.4%) fits Jamnagar's coker complexity, yet reliance on one Angolan stream violates A2 Security Floor thresholds. Execute only as a stopgap while activating A6 Reversibility clauses for alternative Atlantic barrels.

MEMO — Girassol to Jamnagar. Approve CONDITIONAL: 1) Verify A4 sanctions transparency on Angolan supply chain within 48h; 2) Confirm A6 reversibility clause for cargo diversion if API drifts >0.5 points pre-loading. Girassol specs (30.2° API, 0.34% S) align with RIL's 1240 kbd complex; 16,000 kb volume covers only 12.9 days against 15-day baseline, requiring immediate spot top-up. USD LC payment rail active. Net landed cost estimated at $4.20/bbl discount to Brent given high resid (49.4%) yield optimization in DTA zone.

**Proposal:** Divert 45 MMbbl WTI Midland (API 44.5, S 0.32%) USGC→Jamnagar. ETA Day 42.
**Value:** Extends 15-day baseline cover by +36 days; maximizes DTA/SEZ high-complexity yield on light sweet feed.
**Cost:** Premium freight + USD LC liquidity lock; TAN 0.05 preserves catalyst life vs. sour alternatives.
**Constraint:** A3 Concentration Cap limits single-origin exposure; this cargo hits 68% US-sourcing, requiring immediate diversification planning.
**Timing Reality:** Day 20 availability creates a 22-day supply gap before arrival; interim drawdown mandatory.
**Status:** GREEN payment rail confirmed. Execution secures throughput continuity but binds capital until discharge. Immediate approval required to charter VLCCs before rate spike.

MEMO — WTI Midland to Jamnagar. Approve CONDITIONAL: 1) Verify A4 sanctions clearance on USGC supplier within 24h; 2) Confirm A6 reversal clause for freight >$25/bbl spike. WTI specs (44.5° API, 0.32% S) align perfectly with Jamnagar's high-conversion complex. Cargo size (45k bbl) is negligible vs. 1240 kbd capacity, posing zero concentration risk (A3). Green USD LC payment secures A2 floor. Netback positive assuming freight < $22/bbl from USGC. Execution window Day 20 fits 15-day baseline cover without overlap.

Urals (API 31.8, S 1.35%) offers 30 Mb immediate coverage for Jamnagar's 15-day buffer, extending runway to Day 94. Cost: $44.10/bbl under EU Price Cap; total outlay ~$1.32B. Binding constraint: G7 attestation validity on Day 64 amid active Hormuz closure; any insurance gap triggers seizure risk. Timing reality: Cargo arrives Day 64, exactly as baseline stocks deplete. This option buys critical continuity for DTA/SEZ ops at a 15% discount to market, but hinges entirely on A4 (Sanctions Transparency) holding through transit. Failure voids A2 (Security Floor). Reversibility is zero once loaded; traceability must remain unbroken to satisfy A7. Proceed only if legal confirms cap compliance for March 1st loading.

MEMO — Urals-to-Jamnagar Waiver. Approve CONDITIONAL: 1) Supplier attests price ≤$44.10/bbl per EU 18th Package; 2) Charterer confirms no G7 insurance involvement post-cutoff; 3) Cargo segregated in DTA tank farm pending compliance audit. Assay fits Jamnagar coker yield (47% resid, 1.35% S). Volume 30,000 kb covers 24 days, lifting baseline cover to 39 days against 1,240 kbd capacity. Net landed cost estimated $46.50/bbl including freight and waiver premium. Execution required by Day 60 to meet Day 64 arrival.

Draw 18.6 MMbbl from Jamnagar SPR (15-day baseline) to sustain 1,240 kbd throughput for 45 days total. Cost: $1.4B at $75/bbl replacement; margin erosion capped at $4.20/bbl versus spot panic pricing. Binding constraint: A3 Concentration Cap limits single-node exposure to 22% of national demand, forcing parallel coastal draws. Timing reality: Physical release T+4 hours; tanker turnaround T+14 days creates a critical 10-day supply gap before imports resume. This option buys immediate grid stability and prevents DTA/SEZ shutdowns, satisfying A2 Security Floor. Reversibility (A6) requires refilling within 180 days post-crisis. Traceability (A7) mandates real-time inventory logging to prevent diversion. Uncertainty (A5): Closure duration >60 days exhausts strategic buffers without external relief.

MEMO — Strategic Reserve Draw (Jamnagar). Approve CONDITIONAL:
1. Cap release at 280 kbd to satisfy A3 (22.5% concentration limit).
2. Implement real-time API traceability tags per A7 before lift.
3. Define 45-day re-injection schedule to meet A6 reversibility.
4. Publish sanctions exposure matrix for SEZ tranche under A4.
Draw 4.2 Mbbl over 15 days; est. logistics cost $1.85/bbl.

Execute 300 kb/d demand cut paired with product-import swap for 30 days. Net deficit coverage: 9 MMbbl. Cost: $420M premium on swapped cargoes; GDP drag estimated at 0.15%. Binding constraint: A3 Concentration Cap limits single-source swaps to 40%, forcing multi-vendor tendering. Timing reality: 72-hour lag to ratify cuts; 14-day lead time for first swapped cargo arrival. This option buys immediate inventory stabilization without depleting SPR, satisfying A2 Security Floor. Fully reversible (A6) upon Strait reopening. Sanctions exposure (A4) cleared via pre-vetted UAE/Singapore counterparties. Uncertainty (A5) remains on duration of closure; traceability (A7) secured via blockchain bills of lading. Immediate approval required to meet 48-hour deployment window.

MEMO — Demand-side run-cut / product-import swap, 300 kb/d for 30 days. Approve CONDITIONAL: 1) Verify A4 sanctions clearance on swap counterparty within 4 hours; 2) Cap single-source exposure at 15% per A3; 3) Embed A6 auto-reversion clause if inventory dips below security floor. Total volume 9.0 MMbbl; estimated net cost $2.70/bbl including logistics premium.

Divert 2.1Mb owned on-water crude to Kochi (BPCL). Baseline cover jumps from 11 to 18 days immediately. Cost: $4.2M diversion fees + $0.85/bbl demurrage; total exposure capped at $6.0M. Binding constraint: Single-point failure risk at Kochi port exceeds A3 concentration caps unless rail offload accelerates to 95kbd within 72 hours. Timing is critical; vessel ETA is T+4 days. This tranche buys immediate refinery continuity and prevents A2 security floor breach in South India. Reversibility (A6) remains viable until T+24h before port entry. Sanctions status (A4) is clear; no Iranian origin. Uncertainty (A5) lies solely in coastal security clearance delays. Execute now to secure 7-day buffer before national reserves deplete.

Divert 2.1 Mbbl owned on-water cargo to Kochi (BPCL). Extends baseline cover from 11 to 18 days, buying critical runway for diplomatic de-escalation. Hold 2.0 mb VLCC parcel offshore India. Cost: $1.85/day spread + $45k demurrage. Buys 45-day supply buffer against total Hormuz closure, bypassing port congestion. Binding constraint: A3 concentration cap limits exposure to 15% of strategic reserve; A4 sanctions transparency requires immediate cargo provenance audit. Timing reality: Discharge window closes T+12 days post-crisis peak before insurance premiums spike 300%. A6 reversibility allows re-export to Europe if domestic demand softens. This is not inventory; it is liquid optionality. Execute now to lock freight before rates double.
